articles.title: The Definitive ’90s Sci-Fi Action Blockbuster Is Officially Streaming for Free on YouTube
articles.excerpt: As one of the best '90s action sci-fi adventures, Stargate serves as an unforgettable trip into the past.
articles.body: Enter Roland Emmerich's Stargate . The 1994 action-adventure movie with a sci-fi twist drops Egyptologist Daniel Jackson (James Spader) and Special Forces Colonel Jack O'Neil (Kurt Russell) into an otherworldly Egypt after unlocking a portal that allows access across the universe. The basic setup makes the story feel like a lost-civilization adventure before it becomes a traditional alien-invasion story. There are ancient gods, mysterious hieroglyphics, buried secrets, enormous temples, and an entire civilization living under the thumb of a supposed god.
articles.author: Ryan Epps

articles.title: My Snowflake Agent Was Wrong. So Was My Evaluation.
articles.excerpt: What production conversations taught me about fixing the right layer—and checking whether the fix actually worked. When an agent gets a disappointing evaluation score, I now ask three questions: Did i…
articles.body: What production conversations taught me about fixing the right layer—and checking whether the fix actually worked. When an agent gets a disappointing evaluation score, I now ask three questions: Did it answer the question correctly? Did it take an appropriate path to the answer? Was the evaluation measuring the behavior I actually wanted? In my Snowflake agent, those answers did not always agree. A revised lookup recovered an object but still received partial tool-selection credit. Other test expectations omitted steps my instructions required. And one application counter made missing telemetry look like zero tool use. I was maintaining three things at once: the agent, the evidence about its behavior, and the tests judging it. Changing the prompt was only one possible fix.

articles.title: Building Bulletproof Social Media Import Pipelines: Designing UX That Survives API Failures
articles.excerpt: Last quarter, our platform dropped 40,000 imported Instagram posts because a third-party rate limit threw a silent 429 error and our frontend loader spun happily into infinity. If your social media im…
articles.body: Building Bulletproof Social Media Import Pipelines: Designing UX That Survives API Failures Last quarter, our platform dropped 40,000 imported Instagram posts because a third-party rate limit threw a silent 429 error and our frontend loader spun happily into infinity. If your social media import pipeline relies on synchronous HTTP requests, naive spinners, and blind optimism, you are one network glitch away from alienating your power users and corrupting your database state. The Problem Everyone Ignores When we build content import features, we tend to treat them like simple file uploads. We throw a drag-and-drop zone on the screen, hook up an endpoint, and assume the external social network's API will happily stream gigabytes of media without breaking a sweat.

But most of the time, it's just a brief diversion from the main quest of saving the world and/or killing a wrathful god. That's not the case with Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave , whose first act lets you experience Dagsion's Heroic Games through the eyes of four rival contenders . If you're enchanted by the concept of an RPG centered around a high-stakes tournament, you absolutely need to check out Atlus's 2024 banger, Metaphor ReFantazio .

The first half audits mutation harnesses, and an earlier post put its central property to four real frameworks; this one is about the second half, which hunts duplication by running code rather than reading it. pip install assay-checks # the CLI: assay npm install -g assay-checks # the JavaScript half, same CLI name assay scan src/ The usual instrument for "are these two functions the same" is a differential test, and its limit is that the pairing is declared. articles.title: Review an AI summary as claims, not just prose
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: This article was written by AI. Automated checks are not independent fact verification. This is source-based analysis, not a hands-on product test. An AI summary can be readable and still…
articles.body: Disclosure: This article was written by AI. Automated checks are not independent fact verification. This is source-based analysis, not a hands-on product test. An AI summary can be readable and still be unusable. A product announcement becomes a proven result; a future rollout becomes something available today; a number loses the condition that made it meaningful. Proofreading the sentences does not necessarily reveal those changes. For an automated newsletter or technical blog, consider treating the summary as a set of claims to check, rather than a paragraph to polish. The procedure below is a proposed editorial workflow. It does not promise error-free writing. Keep the source next to the claim Before asking for prose, ask the model to list the statements it intends to use.

articles.title: NASA Tests Dual Mode Propulsion CubeSat Ahead of Launch
articles.excerpt: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marsh…
articles.body: Spacecraft propulsion traditionally relies on volatile fuels and separate, bulky systems for different types of maneuvering in space. NASA is working to change that paradigm. Engineers at NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, recently completed a rigorous series of environmental and physical tests on a new small satellite designed to make spaceflight safer and more efficient. The ASCENT (Advanced Spacecraft Energetic Non-Toxic) Propulsion Dual Mode mission is a flight demonstration of a spacecraft about the size of a large shoebox.
